subject: Integration path recommendation and action items (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah@fluxhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration path recommendation and action items (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the procurement/tech review.

Key points from the discovery:
- Primary goal: embed clinical summarization into FluxHealth clinician UI with <200ms p95 per token latency for short prompts, and batch analytics jobs for nightly reports.
- Data sensitivity: PHI in transit, must be encrypted, and customer prefers VPC or on-prem for core patient data; initial POC can use tokenized/filtered payloads.
- Current infra: you are evaluating between continuing with API-based model access (third-party LLM provider) vs moving to dedicated reserved capacity or a VPC-hosted Private deployment. You also have legacy GPU clusters used for research.

Our recommendation based on the call:
1) POC (2–4 weeks): start with Redwood Hosted API using a redacted payload stream to validate prompts and UX quickly (fastest to value).
2) Parallel technical validation: spin up a Dedicated pool for a short trial window (1-week smoke test) to measure latency at scale with your real traffic pattern (prefix caching, batching). Dedicated will show true unit economics and predictable throughput.
3) Production gating: target Private VPC if procurement requires full network isolation and KMS/HSM-managed keys. Private is also the cleanest route for on-prem later.

Action items I propose:
- Red: Redwood to share a short tech checklist (attachments) and a QoS runbook for the Dedicated trial.
- Blue: FluxHealth to confirm whether you can share a tokenized sample payload and a 1-hour traffic window from your cluster for latency profiling.
- Green: Procurement to indicate required contract terms for Private (SLA, data residency, indemnity).

Attachments: redwood-integration-options-one-pager.pdf (high-level), fluxhealth-security-questions-answered.pdf (your completed security Qs with our answers).

Proposed dates:
- Hosted POC kickoff: next Monday, 2026-05-11 (we can provision API keys same day).
- Dedicated smoke run: tentative week of 2026-05-25 (we'll need a short capacity reservation).

If that plan looks good I can loop in Solution Engineering to schedule the setup call.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Next steps from us: we will send the synthetic payload and a 1-hour traffic trace by COB Monday (2026-05-11). Procurement will follow up separately on contract terms.

Hi Sarah / Jonas — quick technical notes from infra/solutions engineering for the smoke test and migration questions: 

- Hosted POC: we support token redaction and prefix stripping. For the POC we can accept synthetic payloads and a traffic replay; that will let us validate latency and response quality without PHI leaving Flux.
- Dedicated: Dedicated capacity provides reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput. For your p95 <200ms target we recommend a 2-GPU pool with A100-class instances and our small-token-optimizations turned on; that'll keep cost reasonable while hitting the latency SLO for short prompts.
- Private / VPC: Private includes a customer-controlled control plane and optional on-prem package. Migration path: we support model artifact export and runtime compatibility—moving from Dedicated to Private is an operational migration (we migrate model versions and configs; there is no proprietary runtime lock-in). If you decide to self-host on your legacy GPU clusters we provide an onboarding bundle (model artifacts + quantization profiles) and a short porting guide.
- Data egress / key management: Private supports customer KMS/HSM and VPC peering; Dedicated can also be configured with VPC endpoints for egress control during the trial.

Can we also get the 1-hour traffic sample in the same format as a single ndjson stream? That format gives us sequence length distribution which is critical for precise kernel selection and batching policy tuning.

If agreed, I'll put together a short runbook for the Dedicated smoke run (what we need to provision, expected metrics, and rollback steps).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
